where I restored ζεούσης [boiling] for νοσούσης [ailing], which had come into the pen of the old scribe because ἰατρός [physician] follows. That word was used by Themistius or. 7 p. 98, where he renders the thought of Aeschylus in these words: φάρμακον δὲ ὀργῆς οἰδαινούσης τὸ μὲν αὐτίκα λόγος ἐστὶν, ᾧ σὺ τηνικαῦτα ἐπράϋνας σφαδά-ζουσαν καὶ ζέουσαν ἔτι [a remedy for swelling anger is at once speech, with which you then soothed it, still throbbing and boiling]. φάρμακον ἀντιζέσεως [a remedy against boiling over] says Clement of Alexandria vol. 1 p. 231, 16. More on this passage I have said in Annot. Oxon. p. 58–60.
The words are suspected of corruption. Schol. ὀργᾷ: τῷ τρόπῳ [he is angry: in his manner]. γρ. (thus Hermann for γάρ) αὐδᾷ, ὁ μάντις δηλον-ότι [he speaks, the prophet, that is].
